summary: Add durable mission-owned dedicated scratch with native final release and bounded dry-run orphan inventory

replay.detail: New scratch acquisitions revalidate their stable activity occurrence and immutable specification against host-local intent and receipt records. Replaying a released acquisition refuses resurrection. Existing missions without scratch declarations keep their current behavior.

schema.detail: Adds the host-local scratch_resources_v1 custody table and host/identity index without changing existing lane admission accounting. Intent, receipt, release tombstone, optional quarantine-handoff state and the last host scan's uninspectable count persist independently of the allocation. No per-consumer ancestry or process-generation evidence is added. Reinstalling an older binary does not remove these records.

rules.detail: Dedicated scratch is consumed only by the owning run's execution tree. Native final-release work follows authored finalizers and positive owner-tree cgroup/scope retirement on success, failure and cancellation. One same-UID host cwd/open-fd scan is defense in depth; hits retain custody, while out-of-contract non-dumpable processes are counted and skipped. Mission deadlines skip final work; inventory remains read-only and no automatic orphan reclamation is enabled.

compatibility.detail: The new typed scratch and inventory operations require an execution host with this implementation. Older hosts do not support these resource operations. Mixed-version execution and downgrade with outstanding scratch custody have not been verified; keep custody-bearing runs on supporting hosts until release is confirmed.

downtime.detail: No additional service restart or coordinated outage is required by this opt-in adapter; restart-to-API and restart-to-health timings were not measured.

manual.detail: Choose an explicitly disposable private dedicated scratch root for new acquisitions. After a mission deadline or interrupted finalization, inspect resources scratch-inventory on the execution host. Unknown ownership or consumers are not authorization to remove a directory.

recovery.detail: Interrupted intent, creation, receipt and release resume through the original acquisition identity under the current host authority. Linux physical removal uses a private no-replace quarantine handoff and verifies the captured allocation before deletion. Restoration intent precedes renaming back, and replay reconciles both locations by inode; mismatch or disappearance never authorizes a release receipt. The single host check uses current kernel cwd/open-fd paths, not per-consumer ancestry history. Non-Linux physical retirement is unsupported and retains custody. Stale generations retain custody. Keep a supporting binary while unreleased records exist; the bounded orphan inventory never deletes allocations, and no fleet-wide recovery policy is enabled.
